title_or_subject: Fort Liscum Military Reservation (Port Valdez, Alaska), established by EO of July 18, 1900, diminished to 659.89 acres. The citing order's heading is Fort Liscum, not Fort Gibbon.

Alaska Orders Index PDF (no Dec 3, 1903 entry; entries 54 = 12/09/1903 Kiska, 55 = 12/31/1903 Liscum)

notes: EO 4131 text (repo OCR, jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4131.txt; ProQuest page blocked by robots): 'FORT I scrm: The entire area reserved by Executive Order of July 18, 1900, as reduced by Executive Order of December 3, 1903. This reservation is situated near Valdez.' So the sentence is about Fort Liscum (OCR 'I scrm'), which follows the Fort Gibbon entry. WPA unnumbered list p.197 (1903 Dec. 31): 'Fort Liscum Military Reservation, Port Valdez, Alaska, established by Executive Order of July 18, 1900, diminished to 659.89 acres. (1907 MR 9; 1910 MR 12; 1916 MR 15; 1904 GLO 465; 1905 GLO 102)'. Neither the WPA list nor the Alaska index has any order dated Dec 3, 1903. Likely EO 4131 prints '3' for '31' (printed error or dropped digit); that is an inference. Text of the 1903 order not found.
